input.question: Those websites that don't let you navigate away from, close, or go to a different page.
input.ground_truth: Web browsers have a few features that allow webmasters to program things to happen when someone tries to leave. They are *intended* to be used for *good*; for example, you have an online word processor, and if you leave before saving your work, it can warn you that it will be lost. But they can also be used for *evil*. It massively pisses off users, so no reputable site would do it, but many sketchy sites have no reputation to lose, so they use it for one last chance to try to sell you something. You may have to click "no" a few times, but the people that make web browsers are aware of this tactic, and after a few they give you an option to ignore any further attempts by the site to keep you there.

Wearing a suit and tie makes me feel confident. What do you think?

It's great that wearing a suit and tie boosts your confidence! Clothing can play a powerful role in how we perceive ourselves and how we present to the world. For many people, formal attire like a suit and tie is associated with professionalism, competence, and self-assurance, which can indeed enhance feelings of confidence in settings like work, interviews, or formal events. 

That said, confidence ultimately comes from within—your mindset, values, and self-acceptance matter most. If this style aligns with your identity and makes you feel empowered, that’s wonderful! It’s all about what works for *you*. If you ever want to explore other ways to cultivate confidence (like posture, mindset techniques, or personal style experimentation), I’m happy to help brainstorm ideas. But for now, rock that suit and own it—you’ve got this! 😊

Answer:

response.prediction: Some websites are designed in a way that you cannot close them, leave the page, or go to another website. This is often done to keep you on the site, sometimes for advertising, phishing, or other unwanted reasons. These types of websites can be annoying or even dangerous because they might try to trick you into clicking something you don’t want to. If this happens, you should try to close your browser using the Task Manager (on a computer) or force quit the app (on a phone), and avoid clicking any buttons on the page.
